title: U.S. House · Kansas's 2nd District
area: Eastern Kansas, including Topeka and southeast Kansas (Pittsburg, Emporia, Ottawa)

context.text: Incumbent Derek Schmidt (R), elected to this seat in 2024 after serving as Kansas Attorney General from 2011 to 2023, defeated Chad Young in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary. Don Coover ran unopposed for the Democratic nomination. The district's 2026 Cook Partisan Voter Index is R+10.

candidates.name: Derek Schmidt
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2025); previously Attorney General of Kansas (2011-2023) and Kansas State Senate (2001-2011)

summary.text: Derek Schmidt is the Republican incumbent representing Kansas's 2nd District, elected in 2024 after more than two decades in Kansas state government. A fifth-generation Kansan from Independence, he served in the Kansas Senate, including as majority leader, and as the state's attorney general for 12 years, and lost the 2022 race for governor. He serves on the House Armed Services, Judiciary, and Small Business committees.

background.text: According to his official biography, he is a fifth-generation Kansan from Independence and graduated from Independence High School, then studied at Independence Community College.

Earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from the University of Kansas, a master's degree in international politics from the University of Leicester in the United Kingdom, a law degree from Georgetown University Law Center, and a doctorate in law from the University of Kansas School of Law.

Worked as an assistant to U.S. Senators Nancy Kassebaum and Chuck Hagel, an assistant to the Kansas Attorney General, special counsel to the Governor of Kansas, and a lawyer with the firm Scovel, Emert, Heasty & Chubb. Also served as a director of Independence Industries Incorporated and the Kansas State Historical Society.
Served in the Kansas State Senate (District 15) from 2001 to 2011, chairing the Senate Agriculture Committee and serving as Senate Majority Leader.

Served as the 44th Attorney General of Kansas from 2011 to 2023, and was re-elected in 2018 over Sarah Swain. According to his official biography, he personally argued three Kansas cases before the U.S. Supreme Court and led efforts to build a new Kansas Bureau of Investigation forensic science laboratory.

Was president of the National Association of Attorneys General from 2017 to 2018 and, according to his official biography, was named the nation's Outstanding Attorney General by his colleagues in 2019.
Won the Republican nomination for governor in 2022, defeating Arlyn Briggs in the primary, and lost the November 2022 general election to incumbent Democrat Laura Kelly.

Elected to the U.S. House in November 2024, defeating Democrat Nancy Boyda and Libertarian John Hauer after winning a five-candidate Republican primary, and took office January 3, 2025, succeeding Jake LaTurner. He won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over Chad Young.
Serves on the House Armed Services, Judiciary, and Small Business committees (2025-2026 assignments).

priorities.text: Border security: cosponsoring and helping pass the Laken Riley Act and Sarah's Law.
Economic relief: curbing federal spending and extending tax relief for Kansas families, small businesses, and farmers and ranchers through the Working Families Tax Cut.
Public safety: legislation to support victims of violent crime, coordinate a federal response to scams targeting seniors, and deport non-citizens convicted of fraud.

positions.summary: Cosponsored and helped pass the Laken Riley Act, backs deporting non-citizens convicted of fraud, and says he supported the One Big Beautiful Bill Act in part because it "fully funded border security and the deportation of illegal aliens."
positions.quote: We locked in tax relief for middle-class families, small businesses, and family farms; fully funded border security and the deportation of illegal aliens; and reduced the growth of federal spending more than ever before in U.S. history.

positions.summary: Voted for the Protecting American Energy Production Act to bar a president from declaring a fracking moratorium without congressional authorization, citing opposition to the prior administration's pause on new oil and gas leases.
positions.quote: Following four years of disastrous energy policy – primarily driven by Executive Orders – this legislation would prohibit the president from declaring a moratorium on the use of hydraulic fracturing (fracking) unless previously authorized by Congress.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary (Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement; Oversight subcommittees), the House Committee on Small Business, and the House Committee on Armed Services (Military Personnel, Readiness, and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees), 2025-2026 assignments.
Voted yes on H.R. 26, the Protecting American Energy Production Act, which bars a president from declaring a moratorium on hydraulic fracturing without prior authorization from Congress.

Cosponsored three public-safety bills - including the Honoring Our Fallen Heroes Act (H.R. 1269) - that were included in the final FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act, which passed the House 312-112 on December 10, 2025 and the Senate 77-20 on December 17, 2025.

candidates.name: Don Coover

summary.text: Don Coover is the Democratic nominee for Kansas's 2nd District and a first-time candidate. Raised on a small dairy farm in rural southeast Kansas, he is a West Point graduate who served about ten years in the U.S. Army and now works as a veterinarian and rancher. He is running on affordability, rural hospital closures, opposition to tariffs, and getting people with working-class backgrounds into Congress.

background.text: Born and raised in rural southeast Kansas, the second oldest of seven children in a family that ran a small dairy, alfalfa, and soybean farm. According to his campaign website, his father was a union truck driver and farmer and his mother a school teacher.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, where, according to his campaign website, he was on the intercollegiate pistol team and was an intramural boxer.
Served in the U.S. Army for about ten years. In his Ballotpedia survey, he says he served as a military intelligence officer and pilot and rose to the rank of Captain.
Earned a graduate veterinary degree from Kansas State University's School of Veterinary Medicine.

In his Ballotpedia survey, he says he runs a beef genetics company providing reproductive technologies for cattle, sheep, and goats, as well as a cattle ranch and a veterinary practice serving local and regional livestock producers.

Advanced from the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for the 2nd District. He describes himself as a first-time candidate, and his campaign site says he is running in part for the future of his granddaughter.

priorities.text: Cites rising grocery and housing costs and the closing of local hospitals as evidence that federal policy is failing working families.
Says he wants people who do hard physical work to be represented in Washington and favors spending within the government's means.

candidates.researchNotes: Coover has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; priorities are drawn from his campaign website's 'Why I'm Running' statement, which does not detail specific issue positions.

candidates.name: John Hauer

summary.text: John Hauer is the Libertarian nominee for Kansas's 2nd District, and also ran in the district in 2024. An Army veteran who describes two deployments to Iraq, he works in a car-battery recycling warehouse and as a delivery driver. He is running on an anti-war, anti-income-tax platform.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Army from 2004 to 2009, and says he is a veteran of two deployments to Iraq.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Kansas State University in 2014.

Ballotpedia lists his career experience as working as a delivery driver. In his survey, he describes himself as a working-class, blue-collar worker employed at a car-battery warehouse where he stacks batteries for recycling and makes deliveries across Kansas, and says he is working with a friend on starting an ice cream business.
Was the Libertarian nominee for Kansas's 2nd District in 2024, finishing third with 4.7% (14,229 votes) behind Derek Schmidt and Nancy Boyda. He was nominated again for 2026.

priorities.text: Wants to end U.S. involvement in foreign wars, close foreign military bases, and bring troops home.
Wants to end the federal income tax without replacing it and sharply shrink the federal government.

positions.summary: Opposes continued U.S. military aid abroad, including to Israel, saying it funds war.

candidates.researchNotes: Based only on his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response; no independent campaign website found.
